purpose: Two invocation-owned foreground fixtures with distinct bundle identities and one byte-identical executable for singleton-safety rehearsal and decision runs.

serialization.json: RFC 8259 UTF-8; duplicate object keys, unknown keys, non-integer numbers, and values outside their declared domains are invalid
serialization.state_file: one compact JSON object; the fixture writes a sibling temporary file without overwrite, fsyncs and closes it, atomically renames it over the destination, reopens it, and requires byte-for-byte readback equality; a partial, missing, oversized, or nonconforming object is invalid
serialization.command_file: exact UTF-8 command token followed by one LF and no other bytes
serialization.integer_domain: unsigned 64-bit integer unless a narrower bound is stated

rules: The primary and secondary bundle identifiers are distinct and exact.
Both bundles contain the same single final FocusFixture executable bytes and therefore the same executable SHA-256.
The role argument, containing bundle identifier, and corresponding Info.plist must agree before the application creates a window or activates.
Neither bundle is a selected-browser-bundle process or an independent helper.
Every named argument occurs exactly once as a name-value pair; pair order is immaterial and no other argument is accepted.
role is exactly primary or secondary.
state and command are nonempty invocation-owned run-local paths of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

Before launch, the court proves state and command distinct, proves their invocation-owned private parent chains contain no symbolic link, and proves both paths remain within the invocation run-local root.

The fixture trusts that court-owned path proof and itself validates only argument shape, nonempty values, the 4096-byte bound, role, and bundle identity; it does not reinterpret path containment as a fixture-side check.
A fixture-detectable CLI or bundle-identity violation exits nonzero before activation, window creation, state publication, or command consumption; a failed court-owned path proof prevents launch.

writer_rules: The court writes the complete command plus LF to a sibling temporary regular file, fsyncs that file, and atomically renames it to the command path.
The court permits exactly one outstanding command file at a time.
The court does not replace, remove, or publish another command until a later state sequence acknowledges the outstanding command.
A pre-existing command destination or sibling temporary file is a protocol failure, never permission to overwrite it.
fixture_rules: The fixture reads at most maximum_bytes plus one and accepts only one exact command value with surrounding ASCII space, CR, LF, tabs, additional lines, prefixes, and suffixes forbidden.
A command is complete and valid only when its syntax is exact and its requested transition is legal in the current lifecycle state.
Only after complete validation does the fixture atomically claim the command by deleting the command file; it performs the requested transition only after that deletion succeeds.
An invalid, partial, oversized, unreadable, or currently inapplicable command remains at the command path and is never executed.

One unchanged rejected command value and failure condition publishes at most one command-rejected state despite repeated polling. The de-duplication is consecutive only: it suppresses a repeat of the immediately preceding rejected (value, failure condition) pair recorded by this process, and it requires no unbounded set of past rejections. A rejected pair that differs in either the value or the failure condition from that immediately preceding pair publishes a new command-rejected state. Only the most recent rejected pair is retained.
close-window is legal exactly once while the sole ordinary window is live; quit is legal while the fixture process is live.

A window-closed or terminating state with sequence greater than the pre-command sequence is the acknowledgement. A command-rejected state is a negative acknowledgement and does not authorize replacement of the retained invalid command.

exit_status.court_rule: The court requires zero only for an expected normal termination and otherwise uses the validated state protocol plus the exact nonzero class; it never treats a nonzero exit alone as a successful lifecycle acknowledgement.
publication_failure_classes: A state object that cannot be JSON-encoded, written, fsynced, renamed, or read back byte-for-byte is a state publication failure and exits 3 by immediate process exit.

A live window whose window number is less than or equal to 0, or greater than 4294967295, cannot be represented in the declared window_shape handle domain; it is a state publication failure and exits 3 by immediate process exit. It is never truncated, clamped, or published as null while ordinary_onscreen_count is 1.

shape.sequence: integer in [1,18446744073709551615], increasing by exactly one for every published state
shape.role: role equal to the CLI role
shape.pid: integer in [1,2147483647] equal to the running fixture process
shape.bundle_id: the exact bundle_identity value corresponding to role
shape.failure_code: state_failure_code exactly when event is command-rejected; otherwise JSON null

window_shape.handle: integer in [1,4294967295] exactly when ordinary_onscreen_count is 1; otherwise JSON null

event_rules.ready: first state; failure_code is null; exactly one ordinary onscreen window exists and its handle is non-null
event_rules.window-closed: acknowledges the sole successful close-window command; failure_code is null; ordinary_onscreen_count is 0 and handle is null
event_rules.command-rejected: failure_code is non-null; no lifecycle transition or activation occurs and the rejected command file is retained
event_rules.terminating: published at most once; failure_code is null; acknowledges a valid quit command or SIGTERM and begins normal application termination

state.publication_scope: run-local only; raw pid, bundle_id, and window handle are forbidden in the external journal and receipt

startup: The application has regular activation policy.
Startup creates exactly one ordinary titled closable window.
Startup calls application activation exactly once, makes that sole window key and frontmost, and then publishes ready.
No code path creates a second ordinary window or performs another activation.
after_close: A successful close-window leaves the application alive with exactly zero ordinary onscreen windows.
The application does not terminate merely because its last window closed.
The application never recreates a window and never activates after close.
termination: A valid quit command and SIGTERM both enter the same idempotent normal application-termination path.
The terminating state is published before requesting application termination.
Repeated SIGTERM or quit observations do not publish a second terminating event or execute termination twice.
Normal quit or SIGTERM exits successfully after applicationWillTerminate completes; an internal publication failure exits nonzero.

A SIGTERM that produces a terminating state is a legal termination confirmation for a close-window command that was already claimed by deletion of its command file: the fixture and the court accept the terminating state, with sequence greater than the pre-command sequence, as that command's acknowledgement. In this ordering the asynchronous window-closed publication may be suppressed because termination is already in effect, and that suppression is not a missing acknowledgement. The independent foreground probe remains the authority for the external disappearance of the window; the fixture's terminating self-report is only the internal consistency signal described by external_observation.authority_rule.

external_observation.ready_boundary: ready proves only the fixture's internal window state; it is not proof that the window server already exposes the window.
external_observation.court_rule: After ready, the court uses the independent foreground probe as the authority for external frontmost and ordinary-window facts and retries within the owning stage deadline until the required external state is observed or the stage fails.
external_observation.authority_rule: Fixture ordinary_onscreen_count is an internal consistency signal only. The foreground probe inventory is authoritative; disagreement is a typed fixture or foreground-observation failure and is never reconciled by preferring the fixture self-report.
external_observation.visibility_rule: Neither the fixture nor the court hides, minimizes, orders out, or otherwise removes the fixture window from the ordinary onscreen set at any point in a passing stage. The fixture's internal isVisible observation is used only as its own live-window signal for choosing between a state with a non-null handle and a state with ordinary_onscreen_count 0; it is never published as, or substituted for, the external onscreen fact, and a stage that only passes because the window was hidden or minimized does not pass.

court_publication.rule: Raw fixture pid, bundle identifier, and handle remain invocation-local. The court validates exact state, reduces those identities with the frozen result-template digest domains, and only then persists whitelisted digests, counts, and booleans with producer court.

primary_direct_inputs: exact single final FocusFixture executable bytes
secondary_direct_inputs: the same exact single final FocusFixture executable bytes
input_digest_ownership.composite_encoding: For each member, compute SHA-256 for the contract, Swift source, build manifest, corresponding Info.plist, and final executable; encode the ordered array of [logical-part-id,sha256] pairs as RFC 8785 canonical JSON; then compute SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 domain agenterm.singleton-safety.v1.frozen-input, one 0x00 byte, and those canonical bytes. The L0 member id is not repeated inside this component array.
input_digest_ownership.same_executable_rule: The final-executable SHA-256 in the primary and secondary composite inputs must be byte-for-byte equal.
input_digest_ownership.one_to_one_rule: The two composite digests populate exactly the existing primary-focus-fixture and secondary-focus-fixture L0 members. Contract, source, build manifest, plist, object files, libraries, bundles, and executable do not become additional L0 members.
